newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods may traumatise young Poles -- government.
newsitem.headline: Floods may traumatise young Poles -- government.

text.p: Poland's worst flooding in centuries may traumatise children who personally witnessed the disaster, a government official in charge of children's affairs said on Sunday.

"They not only saw their homes being swamped by the flood but also watched their toys float away and pets drown," PAP news agency quoted Miroslawa Katna, government commissioner for children's affairs, as saying.
"They often witnessed the extremely brutal behaviour of adults struggling to survive. The destruction of all values before their very eyes cannot but affect their psyche."

Children's reactions may range from deep depression to aggression, but attending summer camps in areas not affected by the disaster has had a therapeutic effect on the young flood victims, Katna added.
Last week the government sent teams of psychologists, social workers and doctors to the hardest hit regions to provide counselling and assistance to those who needed it.
Triggered by torrential rains in early July, Poland's month-long floods claimed 54 lives, swamped 2,600 towns and villages and caused billions of dollars worth of damage.
